title: Deep Space D-6, The Long Way Home, and more Vintage SF Books
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I66Prbdjcn0

On a dreary Sunday with a cup of McDonald's coffee, Daniel (@dungeondive) continues his science-fiction month with Deep Space D-6, the small-box dice game he describes as a board-game FTL, and specifically with The Long Way Home, the free solo RPG module from Tau Leader Games that he says elevates it enormously. Base game first: you roll crew dice and assign them to stations to hold off a threat deck of external ships and internal crises, each threat firing when the turn's d6 matches its numbers. Four ships play differently, and his favourite is the Mono No Aware, whose beam weapon changes effect depending on which crew help fire it and whose equilibrium ability swaps hull and shield values at will.

The Long Way Home reframes all this as a journey. Your mission is done, your jump drive is damaged, and you cross five star sectors toward home, rolling d12s to seed each sector with planets, then turning to numbered book passages with choices, odd jobs, refuelling stations and mini-games. Crew keywords, cargo and upgrade tracks feed back into the story, and every fight is a truncated round of D-6 itself. He compares its effect to what the World Builder did for D100 Dungeon, at a smaller scale, and doubts he will ever play without it.

The video closes with vintage paperbacks: a Brunner with a Dillon cover, Kelly Freas Simaks, Ace sword-and-planet editions, and collector copies of Way Station whose glue is giving out.

----

A free expansion turned a game Daniel nearly sold into one he loves. What fan-made or free module has transformed a game for you?
